title: Deposit Relationship Note: Whether a Restoring Deposit Carries Interest, and Over What Span
content:
Whether the deposit that restores a certificate of the Certificates of Deposit line carries the interest the lost principal would have earned, and the span that interest runs over, turn on the owner's checking relationship and on how often principal left the certificate.

## The grades

Whether the deposit carries the interest the lost principal would have earned is graded: where the owner holds an active checking account of a tier the certificate's own tier lists as qualifying and principal was taken out of the certificate more than once in the twelve months before, the deposit carries simple interest on the loss over the calendar days from the day the last sum left to the day of the deposit; where the owner holds an active checking account of such a tier and principal was taken out only once, the deposit carries simple interest on the loss over the calendar days from the day the term began to the day of the deposit; in every other case, whatever checking account the owner holds and however often principal was taken out, no interest is added.

## What is read

The account is an active account of the bank's Personal Checking line, and the question asked of it is whether its tier appears on the list of qualifying checking tiers the certificate's own tier publishes. The count of withdrawals is taken over the twelve months before the deposit, from the certificate's own ledger.

## Condition and span

| Active checking account of a qualifying tier | Times principal left in those twelve months | Span the interest runs over |
|---|---|---|
| held | more than once | the calendar days from the day the last sum left to the day of the deposit |
| held | once | the calendar days from the day the term began to the day of the deposit |
| held | none | no interest is added |
| not held | any | no interest is added |

The interest is simple: it runs on the loss over the span, and nothing compounds inside it.

## Worked readings, on hypothetical dates

A term that began on 10 January. Principal left on 3 March and again on 18 June. The deposit is made on 1 August.

| The owner's checking account | Span |
|---|---|
| active Premier Checking, the certificate's tier listing it as qualifying | from 18 June to 1 August, principal having left more than once |
| active Everyday Checking, not on the certificate's list | no interest is added |
| none held | no interest is added |

Had principal left only on 3 March, and the owner held a qualifying account, the span would run from 10 January, the day the term began, to 1 August, rather than from the day of that withdrawal.
